```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mulubwa_2020_vancomycin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mulubwa_2020_vancomycin"))$description`
* Article: [Drugs R D 2020;20(2):105-113](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40268-020-00302-7)

# Population

Nineteen preterm neonates (8 male, 11 female) with suspected nosocomial
MRSA infection were enrolled in a randomised double-blind comparison of
two vancomycin brands (Aspen-Vancomycin and Sandoz-Vancocin CP) in two
neonatal intensive care units in Cape Town, South Africa. Every neonate
received 15 mg/kg every 12 h as a 60-min intravenous infusion. Median
(range) postnatal age was 14 (3-58) days, gestational age 31 (23-34)
weeks, postmenstrual age 33 (30-34.7) weeks, birth weight 1.27
(0.63-2.69) kg and current weight 1.48 (0.925-2.62) kg (Mulubwa 2020
Table 1). Neonates with renal dysfunction were excluded. Only trough
concentrations were drawn, before the 3rd, 6th and 9th doses, giving 45
concentrations in total. Parameters were estimated in Monolix 2018R2 by
maximum a posteriori Bayesian estimation, with priors from a published
neonatal vancomycin model fitted to peak and trough data. The same
information is available programmatically via
`rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mulubwa_2020_vancomycin"))$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |

| `lvc` | log(0.884 L) at 1.48 kg | Table 2 'Vd (L)' 0.884 (RSE 24%); Eq. 3 |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.75, fixed | Methods 'Pharmacokinetic Analysis'; Results; Eq. 2 |
| `e_wt_vc` | 1, fixed | Methods 'Pharmacokinetic Analysis'; Results; Eq. 3 |
| `etalcl` | 0.0015987 = log(1 + 0.04^2) | Table 2 BSV CL 4 %CV; footnote b CV = sqrt(exp(SD^2) - 1) |
| `etalvc` | 0.25588 = log(1 + 0.54^2) | Table 2 BSV Vd 54 %CV; footnote b |
| `expSd` | 0.284 | Table 2 residual error 'Exponential' 0.284 (RSE 13.2%) |
| Reference weight | 1.48 kg | Table 1 median current weight; Table 2 footnote a; Eqs. 2-3 |
| One-compartment, linear elimination | n/a | Results 'Pharmacokinetic Model'; Abstract |

| `V = 0.884 * (WT/1.48) * exp(eta)` | n/a | Eq. 3 |
| Exponential residual error `Cc ~ lnorm(expSd)` | n/a | Results 'Pharmacokinetic Model'; Table 2 |
| 60-min IV infusion, 15 mg/kg every 12 h | n/a | Methods 'Vancomycin Dosing, Blood Sampling and Plasma Assay' |

# Virtual cohort

The paper reports current weight only as a median and range. The
virtual cohort draws weight from a log-normal distribution with median
1.48 kg and log-scale SD 0.25, truncated to the observed range
0.925-2.62 kg.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20200302) # weight draw (base R)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20200302) # rxode2 random effects
n_per_arm <- 200

draw_weight <- function(n) {
  wt <- numeric(0)
  while (length(wt) < n) {
    cand <- exp(rnorm(n, log(1.48), 0.25))
    wt <- c(wt, cand[cand >= 0.925 & cand <= 2.62])
  }
  wt[seq_len(n)]
}

cohort <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n_per_arm), WT = draw_weight(n_per_arm))
summary(cohort$WT)
```

```{r model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mulubwa_2020_vancomycin"))
```

# Visual predictive check of trough concentrations (Figure 3)

The study regimen of 15 mg/kg every 12 h (60-min infusion) is simulated
for 9 doses, with trough samples just before the 3rd, 6th and 9th doses
(23.8, 59.8 and 95.8 h, the nominal times of Figure 3 and Table 3).
Simulated observations include the exponential residual error (`sim`
column).

```{r events-helper}
make_events <- function(cohort, dose_mgkg, tau, n_doses, obs_times,
                        treatment, id_offset = 0) {
  doses <- cohort |>
    tidyr::crossing(dose_num = seq_len(n_doses)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      time = (dose_num - 1) * tau,
      amt = dose_mgkg * WT,
      rate = amt / 1,
      evid = 1L
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(-dose_num)
  obs <- cohort |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      id = id + id_offset,
      cmt = "central",
      treatment = treatment
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
```

```{r vpc}
trough_times <- c(23.8, 59.8, 95.8)
ev_vpc <- make_events(
  cohort, dose_mgkg = 15, tau = 12, n_doses = 9,
  obs_times = trough_times, treatment = "15 mg/kg q12h"
)
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_vpc, keep = c("WT", "treatment")) |>
  as.data.frame()

vpc_summary <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    p50 = median(sim),
    p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(vpc_summary, digits = 2,
             caption = "Simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of trough concentrations (mg/L).")
```

Table 3 of the paper gives the observed median trough concentrations
by brand (pooled range 1-19 mg/L):

```{r observed}
observed <- data.frame(
  time = c(23.8, 59.8, 95.8, 23.8, 59.8, 95.8),
  brand = rep(c("Aspen-Vancomycin", "Sandoz-Vancocin CP"), each = 3),
  median = c(11.5, 9, 13.5, 10, 9, 7.5)
)
```

```{r vpc-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Mulubwa 2020: simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of trough concentrations with the observed per-brand medians from Table 3 (points)."}
ggplot(vpc_summary, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_point(data = observed, aes(y = median, shape = brand), size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = trough_times) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Vancomycin trough concentration (mg/L)", shape = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Figure 3 shows a simulated median trough of about 10 mg/L at each
sampling time, a 5th percentile of about 5 mg/L and a 95th percentile
of 15-18 mg/L. The simulated median trough from the packaged model is
about 8-9 mg/L, roughly 15-20% below the Figure 3 median; the
simulated 95th percentile matches Figure 3 and the simulated 5th
percentile is lower (about 3 versus 5 mg/L). Figure 3 was simulated on
the study's own design (each neonate's actual weight and sampling
times), whereas this cohort draws weights from a distribution, which
may account for part of the difference. The observed per-brand
medians in Table 3 (7.5-13.5 mg/L) lie within the simulated 5th-95th
percentile band.

```{r vpc-check}
p50_598 <- vpc_summary$p50[vpc_summary$time == 59.8]
stopifnot(
  # Figure 3 median trough at 59.8 h is about 10 mg/L and the packaged
  # model gives about 8.3 mg/L. A mis-transcribed CL or V (or a missed
  # weight normalisation) moves the median by far more than 30%.
  abs(p50_598 / 10 - 1) < 0.30
)
```

# Steady-state exposure for the current and optimised regimens (Figure 4)

The paper's Monte Carlo simulation compared the study regimen (15 mg/kg
every 12 h) with the proposed regimen (12 mg/kg every 8 h), both as
60-min infusions, reporting AUC0-24h and trough concentration at steady
state. Here each arm is dosed for 10 days and the NCA interval is the
last 24 h (216-240 h), with the trough taken at 240 h.

```{r ss-sim}
obs_grid <- seq(216, 240, by = 0.25)
ev_bid <- make_events(cohort, 15, 12, n_doses = 20, obs_times = obs_grid,
                      treatment = "15 mg/kg q12h")
ev_tid <- make_events(cohort, 12, 8, n_doses = 30, obs_times = obs_grid,
                      treatment = "12 mg/kg q8h", id_offset = n_per_arm)
ev_ss <- dplyr::bind_rows(ev_bid, ev_tid)

sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_ss, keep = c("WT", "treatment")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r ss-pknca}
conc_ss <- sim_ss |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

dose_ss <- ev_ss |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, time == 216) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_ss, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ss, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 216, end = 240,
  auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE
)
nca_ss <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

```{r ss-compare}
reference_fig4 <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("15 mg/kg q12h", "12 mg/kg q8h"),
  auclast = c(366, 440),
  cmin = c(5.88, 9.4)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_ss,
  reference = reference_fig4,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("auclast", "cmin"),
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L", cmin = "mg/L")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Median steady-state AUC0-24h (AUClast over 216-240 h) and trough (Cmin) versus Mulubwa 2020 Results / Figure 4.")
```

```{r ss-attain}
attain <- as.data.frame(nca_ss) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_auc = median(PPORRES),
    pct_auc_ge_400 = 100 * mean(PPORRES >= 400),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(paper_pct = c(`12 mg/kg q8h` = 70.7, `15 mg/kg q12h` = 27.5)[treatment])
knitr::kable(
  attain |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Regimen" = treatment,
      "Median AUC0-24h (mg*h/L)" = median_auc,
      "% with AUC0-24h >= 400 (simulated)" = pct_auc_ge_400,
      "% with AUC0-24h >= 400 (paper)" = paper_pct
    ),
  digits = 1
)
```

```{r ss-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Mulubwa 2020: steady-state AUC0-24h and trough concentration for the current and optimised regimens. Dashed lines: the 400 mg*h/L target and the 8-14 mg/L trough interquartile range the paper associates with it."}
nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_ss) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmin")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    metric = dplyr::recode(PPTESTCD, auclast = "AUC0-24h (mg*h/L)", cmin = "Ctrough (mg/L)"),
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("15 mg/kg q12h", "12 mg/kg q8h"))
  )
ref_lines <- data.frame(
  metric = c("AUC0-24h (mg*h/L)", "Ctrough (mg/L)", "Ctrough (mg/L)"),
  y = c(400, 8, 14)
)
ggplot(nca_wide, aes(treatment, PPORRES)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_hline(data = ref_lines, aes(yintercept = y), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

The steady-state exposures simulated from the Table 2 parameters are
higher than the summaries the paper reports for its own Monte Carlo
simulation (see the starred rows and the assumptions below). The ratio
between the two regimens matches, because both scale with the daily
dose (36 versus 30 mg/kg/day):

```{r ss-ratio}
med_auc <- setNames(attain$median_auc, attain$treatment)
ratio_sim <- unname(med_auc["12 mg/kg q8h"] / med_auc["15 mg/kg q12h"])
ratio_paper <- 440 / 366
c(simulated = ratio_sim, paper = ratio_paper)
stopifnot(
  # AUC is dose / CL, so the regimen ratio is fixed by the daily doses
  # (36 / 30 = 1.2); this is exact up to the weight draw being shared.
  abs(ratio_sim - 1.2) < 0.01,
  # Closed form for the typical neonate: AUC0-24h,ss = daily dose / CL.
  abs(median(attain$median_auc[attain$treatment == "15 mg/kg q12h"]) /
        (30 * 1.48 / 0.102) - 1) < 0.1
)
```

For comparison, the typical neonate's AUC over the first 24 h of
therapy (not at steady state) is computed with a typical-value solve:

```{r first-day}
typical <- data.frame(id = 1L, WT = 1.48)
ev_day1 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_events(typical, 15, 12, n_doses = 2, obs_times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.05),
              treatment = "15 mg/kg q12h"),
  make_events(typical, 12, 8, n_doses = 3, obs_times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.05),
              treatment = "12 mg/kg q8h", id_offset = 1)
)
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
# One single-subject typical-value solve per regimen; rxSolve() drops the
# id column for a single subject, so it is restored from the event table.
sim_day1 <- ev_day1 |>
  split(ev_day1$id) |>
  lapply(function(ev) {
    out <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = ev))
    out$id <- ev$id[1]
    out$treatment <- ev$treatment[1]
    out
  }) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()
nca_day1 <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
    sim_day1 |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment),
    Cc ~ time | treatment + id
  ),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
    ev_day1 |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1, time == 0) |> dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment),
    amt ~ time | treatment + id
  ),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE)
))
day1_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_day1) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPORRES)
knitr::kable(
  day1_auc |>
    dplyr::rename("Regimen" = treatment, "Typical AUC 0-24 h, day 1 (mg*h/L)" = PPORRES),
  digits = 0
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Weight distribution.** The paper reports current weight only as a
  median (range); the virtual cohort uses a truncated log-normal around
  the median. Because CL scales with weight to the 0.75 power and dosing
  is per kilogram, AUC0-24h depends on weight only to the 0.25 power, so
  the choice has little effect on exposure.
* **Monte Carlo summaries not reproduced.** The packaged parameters
  (Table 2, Eqs. 2-3) give a typical steady-state AUC0-24h of
  30 mg/kg x 1.48 kg / 0.102 L/h = 435 mg*h/L for 15 mg/kg every 12 h,
  about 19% above the median of 366 mg*h/L the paper reports for its
  Simulx simulation, and a typical steady-state trough of about 9 mg/L
  versus the reported median of 5.88 mg/L. The target attainment
  (27.5% and 70.7%) is likewise not reproduced: with the 4% CV on
  clearance, almost all simulated neonates exceed 400 mg*h/L. The
  paper's reported spread of AUC0-24h (about 220-630 mg*h/L under the
  current regimen in Figure 4) is also much wider than the 4% CV on
  clearance allows. The model values are kept as published. Two
  observations support the published Table 2 parameters rather than the
  Monte Carlo summary: the observed troughs in Table 3 (medians
  7.5-13.5 mg/L) and the Figure 3 VPC median (about 10 mg/L) are
  closer to the simulated steady-state trough (about 9 mg/L) than to
  the reported 5.88 mg/L, and the AUC over the first 24 h of
  therapy (rather than at steady state) for the typical neonate is
  363 mg*h/L for 15 mg/kg every 12 h, close to the reported 366, and
  408 mg*h/L for 12 mg/kg every 8 h, against the reported 440. The
  paper's simulation settings (sampling of weight, inclusion of
  parameter uncertainty, the dosing day used) are not reported, so the
  source of the difference cannot be confirmed.
* **Supplementary 70-kg normalisation.** The supplementary table
  reports CL = 4.8 L/h/70 kg, which equals 0.102 x (70/1.48) -- linear
  scaling -- whereas Eq. 2, the Methods and the Results all state a
  fixed exponent of 0.75 on clearance (giving 1.84 L/h at 70 kg). The
  model follows Eq. 2. The supplementary V (41.8 L/70 kg) is consistent
  with Eq. 3.
* **Bayesian (MAP) estimation.** The estimates in Table 2 are posterior
  modes obtained with priors from a published neonatal vancomycin
  model; the priors themselves are not reported and are not part of the
  packaged model.
* **Brand.** The two randomised brands were not tested as a covariate
  in the population model, so the model describes both pooled.
* **eGFR units.** Table 1 prints eGFR as 0.28 (0.12-0.51)
  mL/min/1.73 m^2, which matches Eq. 1 evaluated with serum creatinine
  in umol/L rather than mg/dL. eGFR was not retained in the model, so
  this does not affect the packaged model.
* **Specimen.** Samples were collected in serum-separator tubes and
  allowed to clot (serum), though the paper reports 'plasma'
  concentrations.
